subject: Early-output SLA risk assessment + demo action items
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Martin Chen <mchen@velox.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Early-output SLA risk assessment + demo action items

Hi Martin / Sally —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap while it's fresh and a pragmatic set of asks so we can line up a short pilot. High-level notes from our call: 

- Business goal: user-facing assistant where first visible content must feel instant. You emphasized a strict front-door SLO.
- Targeted SLOs (your ask): p50 first-byte ~<120ms, p95 first-byte <=200ms for 75% of production traffic; p95 end-to-end turn <=1.2s for typical 60-token responses.
- Expected load: 300–500 concurrent interactive sessions during peak, ~1M tokens/day for pilot.
- Streaming preference: prefer SSE to start (simplicity with load balancers) but want WebSocket fallback for mobile clients.
- Chunking cadence: you asked whether we can guarantee chunks every ~150–250ms for long responses.

Our immediate proposal and asks:
1) Pilot success criteria: p95 TTFT <=200ms (measured at edge), streaming cadence <=250ms for >90% of chunks, and no client-visible stalls under a 500 concurrent session burst.
2) Technical inputs we need from you by next Tue (2026-12-01): avg prompt length (tokens), avg response length, typical payload size (KB), and whether the UI will buffer partial chunks or render progressively.
3) We'll prepare a pilot checklist (attached) and a draft SLA/appendix for streaming behavior (attached: velox_sla_draft.pdf).

Next steps: we can run a 2-week pilot on a dedicated pool with telemetry dashboards and a joint runbook. Can you confirm the dataset size and the client environments (browser/mobile) so Ben can size concurrency buckets?

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Early-output SLA risk assessment + demo action items

Thanks Sofia — this captures it well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our internal product target is p95 visible first-token <=200ms for our conversational flow (we pushed a little more conservative after the call). p50 ideally <100ms.
- Average prompt length: 18 tokens; typical response length 40–90 tokens depending on the feature.
- Payload sizes: average request ~1.2KB, responses ~3–6KB.
- We plan to render progressively; mobile clients will prefer WebSocket but can fall back to SSE.
- For the pilot we can commit to 1M tokens/day and will route a small percentage of live traffic (can spike up to 400 concurrent sessions).

Procurement note: we need an estimate of expected token cost at pilot throughput and any credits for the trial. Also our security team will push a standard questionnaire (SOC2 items + data retention). We'll send that PDF early next week.

If you can share the concrete probe steps and an initial config we can stand up the pilot environment on our side.

-Martin
Martin Chen
Head of Platform, VeloxAI
mchen@velox.ai

Looping in some tactile options for the pilot configuration and measurement plan — my take: 

- Runtime config: start with an n1-dedicated pool tuned for low-latency (prefill KV cache, continuous batching disabled for first-token-critical paths). Use quantized model variant (q4_0) for baseline cost/latency; we can test q5 later.
- Measurement: p50/p95 TTFT measured at edge (Nginx LB) + server-side histogram. We'll provide dashboards that show inter-chunk gaps (ms) and chunk size distributions.
- Chunk cadence: we can configure the encoder to emit chunks every 150–220ms for average-length responses (40–90 tokens) by pacing token flushing and limiting chunk size to ~60 tokens. That will keep UI incremental updates smooth while controlling RPC overhead.
- Concurrency / capacity: to hold 500 concurrent interactive sessions with the cadence above, initial pilot capacity recommendation = 8 GPUs (A100-class equivalent) with 2x headroom for burst. We'll refine after we see real token distributions.

Action items for the technical kickoff:
1) Priyom: prepare a short runbook for the pilot that lists endpoints, probe scripts, and the measurement keys.
2) Sofia: confirm legal/procurement slack contact and schedule the kickoff meeting.
3) Martin: share the security questionnaire and confirm the client UA breakouts (web vs mobile).

I'll attach a terse probe script later today (will add to the shared Drive link).

Best,
Ben

- I'll schedule a 45-min technical kickoff for Tue 2026-12-01 16:00 PT / 19:00 ET. Please confirm availability.

Attached again: velox_sla_draft.pdf (SLA appendix draft), streaming_probe_instructions.md (probe steps + example curl/ws clients).

Next measurable outcomes for the pilot (deliverables):
- Telemetry: dashboard showing p50/p95 TTFT, chunk-gap histogram, per-session chunk counts.
- Acceptance: p95 TTFT <=200ms measured at edge during a production-like run and chunk gaps <=250ms for 90% of emitted chunks.
- Ops: runbook with escalation path and fallback to a slightly higher-latency but higher-throughput variant if we hit GPU saturation.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
